title: Sara Duterte’s gun ownership presented at impeachment court, but senators unimpressed

items: The prosecution revealed that Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband own a total of 51 guns, valued at approximately P7 million, which were not declared in her Statements of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN).

MANILA, Philippines – The prosecution established before the impeachment court on Monday, September 28, that Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Mans Carpio, own a combined 51 guns, although it’s a fact that senators did not exactly appreciate.

The prosecution’s witness, Philippine National Police firearms office records chief Major Joericson Sangalang, confirmed that 22 guns are registered to the Vice President herself. Alongside her husband’s 29 guns, the firearms have an approximate market value of P7 million.
Rappler first reported about the Duterte family’s gun collection in March 2024.
The prosecution wanted to point out that Duterte did not declare her guns in her Statements of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN).
Senator-judges, however, tried early on to stop prosecutor Bel Zamora’s direct examination of the police official, questioning the testimony’s relevance.

“I have been reviewing my SALN also, and I do not see anything there that says guns,” Senate President Pro Tempore Tito Sotto said, saying he usually includes guns as part of the personal property section.

“Many of us are firearms owners here. We usually put it under personal properties. I don’t see there’s any violation that I feel would happen if they do that, if the Vice President had done that. I don’t think it has that much weight. We’re looking for the bigger evidence that they want to present, if any,” Senate Majority Leader Migz Zubiri added.

In defending the importance of the testimony, Zamora cited 2025 omnibus guidelines on SALN disclosure, which require individual declaration of firearms. Defense lawyer Carlo Narvasa, however, pointed out that the updated rules cannot be applied retroactively.
Post-trial, the prosecution justified its bid to present Duterte’s gun ownership before the court.

blocks.text: Kapunan noted the hesitation of senators to discuss the matters because they are firearm owners themselves, but she believes the prosecution’s presentation shed light on the reality that a public official can have a private army.

“We can also segue into how relevant it is to grave threats (article). They do have a private army, and therefore it makes it more believable and more credible the article on grave threats,” she said. – Rappler.com
